transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A persistent funny smell after cleaning usually points to one of two things: either something organic has gone wrong that wasn't fully removed, or there is an electrical component overheating. Because a burning smell can indicate a serious safety hazard, we need to distinguish between them quickly. Please check:
1. Describe the smell: Is it sour/rotten/mouldy (like old food), or sharp/acrid (like burning plastic or hot metal)?
2. Locate the source: Does it seem strongest coming from the fridge itself? If so, is it near the bottom back (where the compressor and drain pan are) or near the front grille at the bottom? If you smell any burning plastic or see scorching marks on the plug or cable, unplug the fridge immediately and do not use it again until an engineer has checked it. If it smells like food/mould, please let me know where it's strongest so I can guide you to the likely blockage.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

It smells like hot plastic, an electrical sort of burning smell, not rotten food. It's stronger round the back and side of the fridge than inside it. The plug also feels a bit warm, and I sometimes hear a buzzing from the back.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because you have a burning plastic smell, a warm plug, and buzzing from the back, this is an active electrical fault. The most likely causes are a failing compressor start relay, internal wiring insulation breaking down as it heats up, or the compressor itself developing an earth leak. This is not safe to keep using. Please unplug the fridge immediately at the wall socket and do not plug it in again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. Do not try to reset fuses or bypass safety switches. While you wait for the engineer, you can leave the doors closed to help preserve the food. If you need to access internal components like the drain pan or compressor cover, that must be done by the engineer as it involves live electrical parts and sealed systems.

candidates: Spoilt food or mould in the drain pan/filter area (high)
plan: They asked: "Any ideas?" - answer that first.
Checks they have done and what they found: cleaned it out - smell is still there.
The fault they reported is: "funny smell in the kitchen". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
